summary:
The name of this bill is the Employees' Provident Fund (Tenth Amendment) Act, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to further clarify certain defined terms in the prevailing Act, include employees under provincial governments and local levels in the provident fund, and grant authority to the Fund to operate and manage other funds established pursuant to law (Statement of Objects and Reasons, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The bill provides for including employees under the federal government, provincial governments, and local levels in the provident fund (Section 2, Page 1). The Government of Nepal may give necessary directions to the Board of Directors from time to time, and it shall be the duty of the committee to perform work by complying with such directions (Section 9, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 2). The Government of Nepal shall nominate an officer of Gazetted Special Class of Nepal Civil Service as Chairman, three directors from various services of the Government of Nepal, and two directors from banks, financial institutions, and other organized institutions to the Board of Directors, and may remove nominated directors at any time (Section 5, Subsection 2 and 5, Page 1-2). The Government of Nepal shall appoint the Administrator of the Fund, whose tenure of office shall be four years, and the Government of Nepal may remove them at any time (Section 8, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 2). If the Government of Nepal designates the Fund as the operating body of any fund established pursuant to prevailing law, the Fund shall operate and manage that fund (Section 10, Subsection 1, Page 2-3).

Offices and institutions under the federal, provincial, or local level having the liability to deduct fund amounts from the monthly salary of employees pursuant to prevailing law shall deduct and deposit those amounts into the Fund's account (Section 3, Subsection 4, Page 1). An employee depositing money in the Fund may withdraw fund deduction amounts as a loan as determined by the committee (Section 12, Subsection 1, Page 3). If an employee repays the principal and interest of the withdrawn loan or completes the period fixed by the committee, they may withdraw money as a loan again (Section 12, Subsection 3, Page 3). Any remaining principal and interest owed by an employee for a loan taken from the Fund shall be settled by deducting it from the amount accumulated in the Fund in that employee's name (Section 13, Subsection 1, Page 3).

The Board of Directors of the Fund shall consist of seven directors, including the Chairman, three directors from various services of the Government of Nepal, two directors from banks, financial institutions, and other organized institutions, and the Administrator of the Fund (Section 5, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 1-2). The tenure of directors other than the Administrator shall be three years, and after the expiry of the term, they may be re-nominated once (Section 5, Subsection 4, Page 2). The Government of Nepal shall appoint a contributor employee working in a post of at least Gazetted First Class of Nepal Civil Service or 11th level or equivalent of an organized institution as Administrator for a four-year tenure (Section 8, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 2). The Fund may establish branch offices or sub-branch offices (Section 4, Page 1). The Fund may invest in shares of companies working in energy production and transmission, agricultural development, tourism, communication and information technology, and large infrastructure construction jointly with the Government of Nepal or entities owned or controlled by the Government of Nepal (Section 16, Subsection 1, Clause j, Page 3-4). The Fund may operate mutual funds alone or with other institutions, mobilize amounts in capital and financial markets, invest in units of approved mutual funds, private equity funds, and venture capital funds, and make loan investments in housing projects to flow loans to employees for purchasing houses or land plots (Section 16, Subsection 1, 2 and 3, Page 4). If no one bids on mortgaged property during an auction, the Fund itself may acquire such property (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause jh, Page 3). The Board may delegate some of its powers to the Administrator or a sub-committee, and the Administrator may delegate some of their powers to officer employees (Section 17, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 4). The Board may frame necessary regulations and work procedures (Section 18, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 4-5).
